Trevorrow said that it was a "much more involved process with the audience this time".[[200]](#cite_note-Teases-206) In total, the film contains 1,450–1,500 visual effects shots.[[201]](#cite_note-207)[[202]](#cite_note-208)

The film was completed on November 6, 2021.[[203]](#cite_note-209) With a runtime of two hours and 26 minutes, it is the longest film in the *Jurassic Park* series.[[4]](#cite_note-Bell-5) It was initially two hours and 40 minutes, prompting concern from the studio about whether moviegoers would watch such a long film during a pandemic. Trevorrow then worked to shorten the theatrical cut to under 2+1⁄2 hours,[[173]](#cite_note-Collider-June-178)[[204]](#cite_note-210) although he expressed interest in releasing a [director's cut](/wiki/Director%27s_cut "Director's cut") with the deleted footage.[[64]](#cite_note-Taylor-69)

The **Italian campaign** of [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), also called the **Liberation of Italy** following the [German occupation](/wiki/Operation_Achse "Operation Achse") in September 1943, consisted of [Allied](/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") and [Axis](/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") operations in and around [Italy](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy"), from 1943 to 1945. The joint [Allied Forces Headquarters](/wiki/Allied_Force_Headquarters "Allied Force Headquarters") (AFHQ) was operationally responsible for all Allied land forces in the [Mediterranean theatre](/wiki/Mediterranean_and_Middle_East_theatre_of_World_War_II "Mediterranean and Middle East theatre of World War II") and it planned and led the [invasion of Sicily](/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily "Allied invasion of Sicily") in July 1943, followed in September by the [invasion of the Italian mainland](/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Italy "Allied invasion of Italy") and the campaign in Italy until the [surrender](/wiki/Surrender_of_Caserta "Surrender of Caserta") of the [Axis forces](/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") in Italy in May 1945.

*Eucalyptus regnans* is too large for the majority of gardens, but may be suitable for parks.[[65]](#cite_note-Wrigley_1979-65) Propagation is from seed, with the best germination rates being obtained by refrigerating for three weeks before sowing.[[66]](#cite_note-ANPSA-66) Seed may be stored for several years if refrigerated and kept dry. Seedlings are grown in containers but are more prone to damping off than other eucalypts; they are highly susceptible to *[Phytophthora cinnamomi](/wiki/Phytophthora_cinnamomi "Phytophthora cinnamomi")* and *[P. nicotianae](/wiki/Phytophthora_nicotianae "Phytophthora nicotianae")*. Young plants are generally planted out once they are 8 or 9 months old. These are at risk of being eaten by grazing rabbits, wallabies and possums, which can destroy young plantations in severe cases.[[39]](#cite_note-CABI-39)

American horticulturist and entrepreneur Ellwood Cooper noted its rapid growth but demanding soil requirements in his 1876 work *Forest Culture and Eucalyptus Trees*.[[67]](#cite_note-67) *Eucalyptus regnans* requires fertile soil with good drainage and annual rainfall of 1,000 millimetres (39 in) spread over the year, and has poor tolerance to temperatures below −7 °C (19 °F) or drought.[[39]](#cite_note-CABI-39)

Outside Australia, plantations have been successfully established in [New Zealand](/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), [South Africa](/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), [Kenya](/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), and [Tanzania](/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania").[[68]](#cite_note-Borota2012-68)

Up until his death, Milton had been very active, preoccupied with reading, writing articles for religious publications and enjoying his morning walks.
